name: beadhive-default-seats
_comment: bh's DEFAULT seat bundle — what `bh work loop` passes as `--bundle` when the operator
configured none (bh-xrg1f). Without it a dispatched seat resolves baml-harness's
`bare_seat`: permission_mode `plan` plus `closed_rules()` (allow [], ask ['Bash(*)']).
That is correct as a default for an UNKNOWN caller and wrong for this one — a write seat
that can reason but never act burns a full model turn per bead to produce `run_blocked`,
then re-dispatches into the same denial until the loop-breaker fires on attempt count.
DECLARING A MODE ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH. `resolve_bundle_seat` falls back to `closed_rules()`
for any seat that declares no permissions, or declares three empty buckets — so a bundle
carrying only `permission_mode` would still ask on every Bash call, and under headless
`-p` an ask is a refusal. Every seat below therefore declares a real roster.
MODE: `auto` FOR EVERY SEAT, by operator direction (2026-08-12). `auto` auto-approves tool
calls with background safety checks. `plan` was the obvious choice for reviewer/warden and
was rejected deliberately: it forbids writes of every kind, which also blocks tool calls a
reviewer legitimately needs (running the hive's validation writes artifacts). Read-only is
therefore enforced HERE, by the `deny` list, rather than by the mode — see the reviewer
seat. To be re-evaluated once dispatch runs show what each seat actually reaches for.
WHY `deny` CARRIES THE WEIGHT. Claude Code evaluates deny -> ask -> allow without regard to
specificity. Under `auto` an allow entry is a fast path and anything unlisted still gets a
safety-checked approval, so an allow list cannot make a seat read-only; only `deny` can.
`ask` is empty everywhere on purpose: nobody is at the terminal.
NOT A COPY of `dist/bh-<seat>.capabilities.json`. Those rosters are hitch-composed and
read-mostly — they carry no `git commit`, no `git add`, no Edit/Write, and eight `ask`
entries — so a developer seat resolved from one still could not do its job.

developer.description: Implements ONE assigned bead to a reviewable state inside its own bh-managed worktree, then submits.

dispatcher.description: Delivers an epic by coordinating a set of beads on a long-lived branch.

merger.description: Serializes integration of approved beads onto the always-green integration branch.

reviewer.description: Walks an approved branch before the merger lands it. Read-only re: code — does NOT implement or merge.

warden.description: Renders the Assurance verdict on a change. Read-and-block only: no Edit/Write, no merge, no dispatch.
